title: NAFEMS R0027 Test 7 pressurized-cylinder secondary creep
purpose: Verify the global implicit creep procedure against a public structure-level equilibrium and stress-redistribution benchmark while retaining the difference between the published axisymmetric discretization and AgentFEM's current three-dimensional route.
physics: Plane-strain thick cylinder under constant internal pressure with Mises secondary power-law creep

source.organization: NAFEMS; publicly reproduced by Dassault Systemes SIMULIA
source.title: Test 7: Axisymmetric - pressurized cylinder, secondary creep

execution.evidence: The fast gate checks the published radial, hoop and axial steady-state solution. The scheduled structural route applies the elastic pressure preload, advances 1000 hours with an endpoint creep-rate error estimate, and compares raw integration-point stresses with volume-weighted relative L2 norms. A 4 by 8 one-layer Q2 hexahedral quarter sector produced 0.55%, 4.76% and 6.35% radial, hoop and axial errors on Apple Silicon; a 3 by 6 mesh produced 0.97%, 6.39% and 8.63%, so only the declared fine mesh crosses the 8% promotion gate. Halving the time-error tolerance from 5e-4 to 2.5e-4 changed maximum CEEQ by about 1.5e-7 relatively and left the three stress-error measures unchanged to reported precision.

observables: Radial, hoop and axial stress versus physical radius.
Accepted and rejected physical-time increments and endpoint creep-rate error estimates.
Final global residual norm and wall equilibrium.
acceptance: The dependency-free analytical oracle reproduces the published five-radius stress table.
The fine structural result must cross the radial, hoop and axial 8% volume-weighted integration-point error gates and show an improving coarse-to-fine spatial sequence.
Every accepted increment must satisfy the declared endpoint creep-rate integration estimate, independently of Newton convergence.
The elastic pressure preload and subsequent held-pressure creep step remain separate scientific procedures.
The structural calculation remains a scheduled slow gate; the analytical oracle remains in regular CI.
limitations: The structural route extrudes the axisymmetric reference into a fixed one-layer three-dimensional quarter sector because the trusted global creep consumer is three-dimensional; every axial displacement degree of freedom enforces plane strain.

The public Abaqus deck uses four CAX8R radial elements and at most 40 increments. AgentFEM currently uses a quadratic hexahedral three-dimensional route and permits up to 220 accepted increments; agreement in stress is verified, but execution efficiency is not claimed equivalent.
Two endpoint-rate tolerances provide a terminal-time refinement check; richer transient-history convergence remains a separate obligation when intermediate-time response is used.
